excavators.specific: Construction and earthmoving contractors are the primary excavator buyers. Lenders like excavators because they hold value well and have a strong secondary market—Caterpillar, Komatsu, and John Deere models retain 50–70% of value after 5 years. Project-based revenue is common; lenders may ask for contract backlog or seasonal revenue patterns. Mini excavators (under 6 tons) often finance more easily than large machines due to lower ticket size and broader buyer demand.

bulldozers.specific: Bulldozers are used in construction, mining, land clearing, and agriculture. Crawler dozers (Caterpillar D6, D8, etc.) hold value better than wheel dozers. Lenders favor established contractors with consistent project pipelines. Mining and heavy civil contractors often need larger machines; smaller operations use compact dozers. Depreciation is predictable, which supports financing. Used bulldozers 5–7 years old are commonly financed with shorter terms.

wheel-loaders.specific: Wheel loaders serve construction, quarries, landscaping, and material handling. Compact loaders (1–2 cu yd) suit small contractors; large loaders (4–6+ cu yd) serve mining and aggregates. Brands like Caterpillar, Volvo, and John Deere dominate. Lenders treat wheel loaders similarly to excavators—strong resale, established market. Quarry and aggregate operations often bundle loaders with haul trucks; combined financing can improve terms.

backhoes.specific: Backhoe loaders combine a loader bucket with a rear excavator arm—versatile for contractors doing utility work, small excavation, and site prep. Lower ticket size ($40K–$120K) means quicker approvals and broader lender acceptance. John Deere, Caterpillar, and Case are common. Ideal for utility contractors, landscapers, and small earthmoving outfits. Used backhoes are widely available; lenders typically finance units up to 7 years old.

skid-steers.specific: Skid steers are compact, agile loaders used in construction, landscaping, agriculture, and rental. Bobcat, Caterpillar, and John Deere lead the market. Lower cost and high versatility make them popular with small contractors and rental fleets. Lenders view them favorably—strong demand, predictable resale. Attachment financing (buckets, augers, grapples) can sometimes be bundled. Rental companies often use lease structures to cycle equipment.

mini-excavators.specific: Mini excavators (under 6 tons) suit urban construction, landscaping, and utility work where full-size machines cannot fit. Kubota, Bobcat, and Yanmar are popular. Lower cost and high demand make them easier to finance than large excavators. Many first-time equipment buyers start with minis. Residential contractors and landscapers are primary buyers. Used minis 3–5 years old retain value well.

dump-trucks.specific: Dump trucks are essential for construction, aggregates, and hauling. Class 8 dump trucks and vocational chassis (Peterbilt, Kenworth, Mack) dominate. Lenders evaluate trucking revenue, route stability, and maintenance history. Owner-operators and small fleets are common buyers. Used dump trucks are widely financed; lenders prefer trucks under 7 years with documented maintenance. Hauling contracts can strengthen applications.

semi-trucks.specific: Semi-truck financing is a specialized niche. Lenders assess freight revenue, ELD data, and fleet utilization. Owner-operators and small carriers are primary borrowers. New sleepers and day cabs both qualify; used trucks 3–5 years old are commonly financed. Trucking-specific lenders often offer better terms than general equipment lenders. See trucking business financing for industry context.

box-trucks.specific: Box trucks serve delivery, moving, and last-mile logistics. Lower cost than semis; lenders view them as straightforward. FedEx-style and walk-in van bodies are common. Delivery companies and moving businesses are primary buyers. Used box trucks 5–7 years old are frequently financed. Lenders look for consistent delivery or route revenue.

forklifts.specific: Forklifts serve warehouses, manufacturing, and distribution. Electric vs propane affects upfront cost; electric has lower operating cost. Toyota, Crown, Raymond, and Hyster dominate. Lenders like forklifts—high volume market, predictable resale. Multi-unit deals (replacing a fleet) can secure better terms. Lease structures are popular for companies that cycle equipment every 5–7 years.

tractors.specific: Agricultural tractors are financed through equipment lenders and ag-specific programs. John Deere, Case IH, and AGCO dominate. Crop farmers, cattle operations, and custom harvesters are primary buyers. Seasonal revenue is normal; lenders may structure payments around harvest. Used tractors retain value; 5–10 year old units are commonly financed. Ag lenders often offer longer terms (7+ years) for large equipment.

combines.specific: Combines are high-ticket ag equipment. John Deere and Case IH lead. Custom harvesters and large row-crop farmers are primary buyers. Financing terms often extend to 7+ years; down payments of 10–20% are common. Ag lenders specialize in combines; they understand seasonal cash flow and harvest cycles. Used combines 3–5 years old are frequently financed with ag programs.

dental-equipment.specific: Dental practices finance chairs, units, CEREC systems, and digital scanners. Technology refresh cycles (every 5–8 years) make leasing attractive. Many healthcare equipment lenders specialize in dental; they understand operatory buildouts and bundled packages. DSOs (dental support organizations) often finance multi-location rollouts. Vendor programs (Dentsply, Planmeca) may offer promotional terms.

medical-imaging.specific: MRI, CT, X-ray, and ultrasound systems are high-value medical equipment. Healthcare equipment lenders and manufacturer captive finance (Siemens, GE, Philips) dominate. Practices and imaging centers are buyers. Technology obsolescence drives shorter useful life; leases with upgrade options are common. Used imaging equipment is financed but may have shorter terms. Down payments of 10–20% are typical for larger systems.

restaurant-refrigeration.specific: Walk-in coolers, freezers, and reach-in units are essential for restaurants. Refrigeration holds value; lenders finance it readily. Restaurant revenue is often seasonal or variable; lenders may focus on average monthly deposits. Used refrigeration is common; 3–5 year old units are frequently financed. Vendor programs from refrigeration suppliers sometimes offer 0% or low-rate promotions.

cnc-machines.specific: CNC machining centers, lathes, and mills serve manufacturing and job shops. Haas, Mazak, and DMG MORI are common. Job shops often have project-based revenue; lenders assess backlog and industry stability. Used CNCs 5–8 years old are financed; precision and condition matter. Manufacturing lenders understand depreciation and technology cycles. Multi-machine deals can improve terms.

pos-systems-restaurant.specific: POS systems for restaurants include terminals, tablets, and integrated software. Lower ticket size means quick approvals. Lenders and vendor programs (Toast, Square) often offer 0% or low-rate promotions. Multi-location rollouts can bundle POS with other restaurant equipment.

alignment-racks.specific: Alignment racks and machines are used by auto shops for wheel alignment. Hunter and John Bean are common brands. Lenders treat them as standard shop equipment; strong resale. Independent shops and tire centers are primary buyers. Often bundled with diagnostic and tire equipment.

injection-molding.specific: Injection molding machines produce plastic parts for manufacturing. Brands like Engel, Arburg, and Haitian dominate. High-ticket machines; lenders assess manufacturing revenue and capacity utilization. Used equipment 5–10 years old is commonly financed. Mold tooling can sometimes be bundled.

landscape-trailers.specific: Landscape and equipment trailers carry mowers, skid steers, and tools. Lower cost; quick approval. Landscapers and contractors are primary buyers. Often financed with the equipment they carry. Used trailers 3–5 years old are commonly financed.

refrigerated-trucks.specific: Refrigerated trucks and reefers haul perishables for food distribution and logistics. Truck + reefer unit can be financed together. Lenders evaluate delivery routes, contract stability, and cold-chain revenue. Used reefers 5–7 years old are financed; temperature control certification matters.

dock-equipment.specific: Dock levelers, plates, and truck restraints support warehouse loading. Often bundled with conveyor or forklift purchases. Lenders treat dock equipment as standard warehouse capital. Distribution centers and manufacturers are buyers. Used dock equipment is less common but financed when available.

stump-grinders.specific: Stump grinders remove tree stumps for arborists and landscapers. Bandit, Vermeer, and Rayco are common. Seasonal revenue is normal; lenders may structure around tree-service cash flow. Compact tow-behind units finance more easily than large self-propelled machines.

industrial-robots.specific: Industrial robots automate welding, assembly, and material handling. Fanuc, ABB, and KUKA dominate. Lenders assess manufacturing ROI and integration timelines. Used robots 3–5 years old are financed; controller and reach capacity affect value. Automation lenders understand payback periods.

surgical-equipment.specific: Surgical tables, lights, and procedure equipment serve hospitals and ASCs. Healthcare equipment lenders specialize in this niche. Technology refresh and regulatory compliance drive upgrade cycles. Bundled OR packages can improve terms. Used surgical equipment is financed with shorter terms.

brake-rotor-equipment.specific: Brake lathes, lathes, and rotor equipment serve auto shops. Hunter and ProCut are common. Standard shop equipment with predictable resale. Often financed with other shop tools. Independent shops and chains are buyers. Used equipment 3–5 years old is commonly financed.

commercial-kitchen.specific: Ranges, ovens, griddles, and fryers form the backbone of restaurant kitchens. Lenders finance commercial kitchen equipment readily—essential for restaurant operations. Vendor programs (Wells, Follett) often offer promotional terms. Full kitchen buildouts can bundle equipment; new locations and remodels are common use cases.

press-brakes.specific: Press brakes bend sheet metal for fabrication shops. Amada, Cincinnati, and Trumpf are common. Job shops and metal fabricators are buyers. Lenders treat them like CNC equipment—strong secondary market. Used press brakes 5–8 years old are financed. Tooling can be bundled.

sprayers.specific: Ag sprayers apply fertilizer and pesticide. John Deere, Case IH, and Hagie dominate. Seasonal farm revenue; lenders may align payments with harvest. Custom applicators and row-crop farmers are buyers. Used sprayers 3–5 years old retain value. Ag-specific lenders offer longer terms.

dishwashers-warewashing.specific: Commercial dishwashers and warewashing systems serve restaurants and hospitality. Hobart and Meiko are common. Essential for health compliance; lenders finance readily. Often bundled with commercial kitchen or refrigeration. Low ticket; quick approval. Used units 3–5 years old are financed.

exam-procedure-equipment.specific: Exam tables, procedure chairs, and specialty equipment serve medical practices. Healthcare lenders specialize in this niche. Often bundled with imaging or surgical equipment for new practices. Technology refresh cycles drive upgrades. Used exam equipment is financed when in good condition.

pallet-jacks.specific: Manual and electric pallet jacks are low-cost warehouse equipment. Crown, Toyota, and Raymond are common. Very quick approval; often bundled with forklifts or conveyor. Warehouses and distributors buy in quantity. Leasing is popular for fleets.

trailers.specific: Flatbed, enclosed, and utility trailers serve hauling and logistics. Lower ticket; broad lender acceptance. Owner-operators, contractors, and landscapers are buyers. Often financed with the truck. Used trailers 3–5 years old are commonly financed.

tanker-trucks.specific: Tanker trucks haul fuel, chemicals, and liquids. Specialized equipment; lenders assess hazmat compliance and contract stability. Fuel haulers and chemical transporters are primary buyers. Used tankers 5–7 years old are financed; tank certification matters.

scanning-wms.specific: Barcode scanners and WMS software support warehouse operations. Often bundled with hardware and conveyor. Lenders treat it as IT/equipment hybrid; software can be financed with hardware. Distribution and e-commerce fulfillment are primary use cases.

tire-changers-balancers.specific: Tire changers and balancers are standard auto shop equipment. Hunter and Coats are common. Often bundled with alignment or brake equipment. Independent shops and tire chains are buyers. Low ticket; quick approval. Used equipment 3–5 years old is financed.

shop-tools-storage.specific: Shop tools, tool chests, and storage systems serve auto and repair shops. Snap-on and Matco have financing programs. General equipment lenders also finance tool packages. Often bundled with lifts and diagnostic equipment. Used tool sets are less common but financed.

hay-balers.specific: Hay balers produce round or square bales for cattle and horse operations. John Deere, New Holland, and Vermeer dominate. Seasonal revenue; lenders may structure around hay season. Livestock and hay producers are buyers. Used balers 5–7 years old retain value.

pallet-racking.specific: Pallet racking and warehouse storage systems support distribution. Often bundled with forklifts and conveyor for new buildouts. Lenders treat storage as standard warehouse capital. Used racking is commonly financed. Expandable systems can be financed in phases.

bucket-trucks.specific: Bucket trucks (aerial work platforms) serve utilities, tree services, and telecom. Altec and Terex are common. Lenders assess contract revenue from utilities or tree work. Used bucket trucks 5–7 years old are financed; boom inspection and certification matter.

auto-lifts.specific: Two-post and four-post auto lifts are essential for shops. Rotary, BendPak, and Mohawk are common. Low ticket; very quick approval. Independent shops, dealerships, and fleets are buyers. Often bundled with alignment and tire equipment. Used lifts are financed when certified.

prep-equipment-restaurant.specific: Prep tables, slicers, mixers, and food prep equipment serve restaurant kitchens. Often bundled with commercial kitchen or refrigeration. Low to moderate ticket; quick approval. New locations and kitchen remodels drive demand. Vendor programs may offer promotional terms.

ventilation-hood-systems.specific: Commercial hoods and ventilation are required for restaurant kitchens. Often bundled with commercial kitchen equipment. Lenders treat them as essential kitchen capital. Health and fire code compliance drives demand. New buildouts and remodels are common use cases.

log-trucks.specific: Log trucks haul timber for forestry and sawmills. Specialized chassis and trailers; lenders assess logging contracts and timber revenue. Seasonal factors apply. Used log trucks 5–7 years old are financed. Forestry-specific lenders may offer better terms.

commercial-mowers.specific: Commercial walk-behind and riding mowers serve landscapers and grounds crews. Exmark, Scag, and Toro are common. Seasonal revenue is normal. Often financed with zero-turns and other lawn equipment. Used mowers 3–5 years old retain value. Multi-unit deals can improve terms.

diagnostic-equipment-auto.specific: OBD scanners and diagnostic tools serve auto shops. Snap-on, Autel, and Launch are common. Often bundled with lifts and alignment. Low ticket; quick approval. Technology refresh drives upgrades. Independent shops and dealerships are buyers.

conveyor-systems.specific: Conveyor systems move goods in warehouses and fulfillment centers. Often part of larger automation projects. Lenders assess distribution revenue and throughput. Used conveyor 3–5 years old is financed. Can be bundled with WMS, pallet racking, and forklifts.

grain-equipment.specific: Grain bins, augers, and handling equipment serve farms and elevators. Ag lenders specialize in grain equipment. Seasonal harvest revenue; payments may align with crop sales. Used grain equipment 5–10 years old is financed. Often bundled with tractors and combines.

lab-equipment-medical.specific: Lab analyzers, centrifuges, and diagnostic equipment serve clinical labs and practices. Healthcare equipment lenders specialize. Technology refresh and regulatory compliance drive upgrades. Used lab equipment 3–5 years old is financed. Often bundled with imaging or surgical equipment.

flatbed-trucks.specific: Flatbed trucks haul construction, machinery, and oversized loads. Lenders evaluate freight revenue and route stability. Owner-operators and small carriers are buyers. Used flatbeds 5–7 years old are financed. Often grouped with dump trucks and specialized hauling.

zero-turn-mowers.specific: Zero-turn mowers are popular with landscapers and property managers. Exmark, Scag, and Gravely dominate. Lower cost; quick approval. Often financed with commercial mowers and other lawn equipment. Used zero-turns 3–5 years old retain value. Seasonal revenue is normal.

diagnostic-devices-medical.specific: ECG, vital sign monitors, and point-of-care devices serve medical practices. Healthcare lenders finance diagnostic devices readily. Often bundled with exam or imaging equipment. Technology refresh drives upgrades. Used devices 3–5 years old are financed when compliant.

lathes-milling-machines.specific: Manual and CNC lathes and mills serve job shops and manufacturing. Haas, Mazak, and Okuma are common. Lenders treat them like CNC equipment. Job shops often have project-based revenue. Used lathes and mills 5–10 years old are financed. Tooling can be bundled.
